gaps.sentence: The moment ___ she saw the results, she burst into tears.
gaps.explanation: 'When' links the moment to the action; 'where' and 'why' do not fit a time noun.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: The Eiffel Tower, ___ attracts millions of visitors, was completed in 1889.
gaps.explanation: For things in non-defining clauses use 'which'; 'that' is not allowed after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The river ___ runs through the town often floods in spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is the subject relative pronoun for things and animals.

gaps.sentence: The police have arrested the man ___ stole the painting.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun for people in defining clauses.
